findings.summary: The public UI is hard-coded light and does not honor the user’s dark-theme preference.
findings.evidence: The default and dark-emulated 360px screenshots are pixel-identical; the computed root color-scheme is “normal”.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and retint surfaces, text, borders and imagery under prefers-color-scheme, following the dark-mode guidance.

findings.summary: Essential footer links do not remain sufficiently distinct at normal contrast, so higher-contrast needs are not met.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 2.86:1 for 11px blue footer links against #d0d0d0.
findings.suggestedFix: Use tokens that meet WCAG contrast in the default palette and add forced-colors/prefers-contrast treatment.

findings.summary: Route changes are abrupt rather than preserving spatial continuity.
findings.evidence: DOM/script inspection found no authored View Transition use; navigation is conventional full-document links and no animations were active.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for same-origin catalogue navigation, with reduced-motion safeguards.

findings.summary: The long homepage provides no position-aware navigation or scroll progress.
findings.evidence: The page is 2,882px tall, while screenshots and DOM show static header/chrome and no active scroll-linked behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact sticky header or progress/return affordance that responds to scroll state without obscuring content.

findings.summary: A representative listing is served as a desktop-only 980px canvas and scaled down on phones.
findings.evidence: At a 360px viewport the listing had no viewport meta, a 980px layout viewport and 0.367 scale; text and controls are tiny.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve one responsive HTTPS template with a viewport meta tag, intrinsic sizing and fluid/container-aware layout.

findings.summary: Reusable catalogue components do not adapt cleanly across available space.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found zero container rules; desktop cards stretch to 780px rows, while the listing falls back to a fixed desktop canvas on mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Give cards intrinsic limits and container-query variants rather than relying on separate fixed-width templates.

findings.summary: Several common links are below the recommended touch-target size.
findings.evidence: The focus/target probe measured login and registration at 45×31px, primary search links at 38px high, and category links at 32px high. Keyboard outlines were visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive target boxes to at least 44×44 CSS pixels while preserving visible focus.

findings.summary: Guest users receive a generic, unactionable system error on the homepage.
findings.evidence: Both desktop and mobile screenshots show “システムエラーが発生しました。” with no cause, retry, dismissal or recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the generic toast with a contextual message, a retry or alternative next step, and accessible status announcement.

findings.summary: Cold-load rendering is slow despite a quiet main thread.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 4.8s and FCP 4.1s; the raw trace measured LCP/FCP 3.33s with no blocking tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce TTFB/render delay and prioritize the 20th-anniversary LCP image with fetchpriority=high after confirming it remains the LCP candidate.

findings.summary: Parser-blocking resources and weak cache delivery delay the first view.
findings.evidence: HAR identified three VeryHigh parser-inserted stylesheets and two synchronous parser scripts; its hygiene section flags major sprites, JS, CSS and font responses without useful cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, defer noncritical scripts, and give versioned static assets long-lived immutable caching.

findings.summary: The page ships avoidable unused code and duplicate sprite cost.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 42KiB unused JS and 35KiB unused CSS; HAR shows near-duplicate 181KiB sprite transfers from sp.mbga.jp and ava-a.sp.mbga.jp.
findings.suggestedFix: Split page-specific code and serve each shared sprite once from one canonical asset origin.

findings.summary: Important controls and form fields lack robust accessible names and labels.
findings.evidence: The homepage has no landmarks and a visible menu button without text; the login email/password inputs rely on placeholders and have no associated labels; the image probe found 44 images without alt in the rendered DOM, many hidden drawer assets.
findings.suggestedFix: Add persistent labels, accessible button names, semantic landmarks, and empty or descriptive alt according to image purpose.

findings.summary: Footer text contrast fails WCAG minimums.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 2.86:1 contrast for multiple 11px footer links where 4.5:1 is required.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken link color or lighten its background and verify all states at 4.5:1 or better.

findings.summary: The homepage lacks navigation/main landmarks and includes many script-only pseudo-links.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found no main/nav/header/footer landmarks; Lighthouse failed landmark-one-main; numerous anchors use javascript:void(0). Focus rings are visible, but structure is weak.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce semantic page landmarks and real anchors/buttons while retaining the native focus outline.

findings.summary: User zoom is disabled and one core template does not reflow.
findings.evidence: Two homepage viewport tags and the login viewport specify maximum-scale=1,user-scalable=no; the listing has no viewport meta and renders at 980 CSS pixels on a 360px device.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove scaling restrictions and rebuild the listing to reflow at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Legacy platform choices create fragile navigation and maintenance risk.
findings.evidence: The listing loads jQuery 1.7.2 and Modernizr 2.5.3, uses HTTP canonical/assets after redirect, and the homepage contains many javascript:void(0) anchors.
findings.suggestedFix: Retire legacy libraries, use native platform APIs and real href/button semantics, and keep all authored asset URLs HTTPS.

findings.summary: A substantial set of navigation actions is not crawlable, and the listing is not mobile-friendly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors for javascript:void(0) links; the listing has no viewport meta and is scaled from 980px.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href URLs for navigation and a responsive viewport/template on every public listing.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap signals are inconsistent across hosts and templates.
findings.evidence: The rendered homepage has no canonical; the listing canonical is HTTP www.mbga.jp; requests to sitemap.xml resolved to generic Mobage HTML rather than a sitemap.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose one HTTPS canonical host, emit self-consistent canonical URLs, and publish a valid sitemap that matches robots/indexing policy.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but cookies and response headers are not safely hardened.
findings.evidence: All three guest cookies lack Secure and use SameSite=None; the document lacks CSP, HSTS and X-Content-Type-Options.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure and appropriate SameSite/HttpOnly attributes, then deploy HSTS, nosniff and a tested CSP.

findings.summary: Guest loads include advertising/analytics collection without an evident minimisation explanation in the audited path.
findings.evidence: Network evidence includes ad-a.sp.mbga.jp and an analytics JSON-RPC call; the login DOM embeds an analytics endpoint/tracking cookie plus reCAPTCHA/Yahoo tags.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory guest telemetry, remove unnecessary calls, batch essential analytics and disclose/control third-party processing.

findings.summary: Authentication remains password-centric and does not expose a phishing-resistant passkey option.
findings.evidence: The login page offers password and social providers; the probe found no authored WebAuthn use, despite browser support. No permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey registration/sign-in alongside existing recovery paths and request permissions only after a user action.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Header inspection found no frame protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy in addition to missing CSP/HSTS/nosniff.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy frame-ancestors, strict Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, then verify compatibility.

findings.summary: Failure routing does not produce a clear recoverable state.
findings.evidence: A deliberately unknown URL loaded generic Mobage content with no not-found explanation; the homepage also emitted an unactionable system error.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a proper 404 page with useful navigation, and make runtime/network failures explicit with retry and safe fallback actions.

findings.summary: The authentication document does not identify its Japanese language.
findings.evidence: The login probe found an empty html lang value while the visible interface is Japanese; the homepage correctly uses lang=ja.
findings.suggestedFix: Set lang="ja" (and dir where needed) on every document and use logical CSS properties for translation-safe layout.

findings.summary: The login form lacks client-visible validation semantics before reCAPTCHA submission.
findings.evidence: Email and password fields are not required, have no aria-invalid/aria-describedby relationship, and expose no persistent labels; the homepage error is generic and unrecoverable.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, connect concise field errors programmatically, preserve entered values, and announce the summary.

findings.summary: Login fields do not use purpose-specific autofill tokens.
findings.evidence: Email uses autocomplete="on" and password has no autocomplete token; neither uses username/current-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete="username" and autocomplete="current-password" and keep labels visible.

findings.summary: The page relies heavily on legacy PNG/GIF assets and eagerly loads below-fold images.
findings.evidence: Image inspection found 39 legacy-format images, no modern-format images and 16 below-fold images without lazy loading; images account for 1,001,309 transferred bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Convert suitable imagery to AVIF/WebP, preserve dimensions, add responsive sources and lazy-load noncritical below-fold images.

findings.summary: Image sprites and multi-origin delivery dominate a 1.16MB guest load.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 67 requests and 1,160,179 transferred bytes; five large PNG sprites total roughly 767KB and 61 requests were classified off the requested origin.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a template-specific byte budget, remove duplicate sprites, defer nonessential assets and consolidate same-site delivery.

taskList.title: Harden cookies and browser security headers
Restore zoom, responsive listing reflow and adequate targets
Repair labels, landmarks, contrast and semantic navigation
Make errors and missing routes explicit and recoverable
Cut LCP delay, parser blocking and duplicate unused payload
Fix canonical host, sitemap and crawlable route signals
Add dark theme and preference-aware contrast
Retire legacy libraries and abrupt route behavior
